beats.text: Your phone just buzzed. It didn't.
In one survey, almost nine out of ten students had felt a phantom vibration.
For most, it happens every now and then. And most don't find it bothersome.
Your brain is on alert for one signal. So it reads a twitch, or your shirt, as a buzz.
Researchers call it a tactile hallucination. And it's incredibly common.
Your brain isn't broken. It's just listening too hard.

sources: Drouin, Kaiser & Miller (2012). Phantom vibrations among undergraduates. Computers in Human Behavior 28. ~89% reported phantom vibrations; typically about every two weeks; most not bothered.
Rothberg et al. (2010), BMJ: phantom vibration as a tactile hallucination among medical staff. Via Wikipedia 'Phantom vibration syndrome'.
